tower-of-hanoi.title: Free blocked larger disks by moving top smaller disks first
tower-of-hanoi.principle: If a larger disk you need to move is not the topmost on its peg, first relocate any smaller disks that are on top of it.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever you need to move a disk that is not currently the top disk of its source peg.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Attempting to move a larger disk while smaller disks remain above it on the same peg.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Validate source peg before each move
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Check that the disk you intend to move is actually the topmost disk on its source peg.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moving a disk from a peg where a smaller disk is on top, causing a source‑top mismatch.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Validate destination peg before each move
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Ensure the destination peg is empty or its topmost disk is larger than the moving disk.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Placing a larger disk onto a peg whose top disk is smaller, violating size ordering.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Apply classic Hanoi recursion to generate move sequence
tower-of-hanoi.principle: To transfer a contiguous stack of k disks from one peg to another, recursively move the top k‑1 disks to the auxiliary peg, move the largest disk, then move the k‑1 disks onto the target.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When you have a clean stack of consecutive disks on a single peg that needs to be moved as a unit.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Trying to move a whole sub‑stack without using the recursive decomposition, leading to an incomplete or illegal sequence.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Clear destination peg of smaller disks before moving larger disk
tower-of-hanoi.principle: If the destination peg has a smaller disk on top, move that smaller disk elsewhere before placing the larger disk onto the peg.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever you are about to place a larger disk onto a peg that already contains disks.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Attempting to move a large disk onto a peg where a smaller disk blocks the placement.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Validate final configuration after move generation
tower-of-hanoi.principle: After constructing the move list, simulate the moves from the initial state and verify that the resulting configuration matches the goal.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: After you have generated the full sequence of moves, before outputting it.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Skipping the final simulation and outputting a move list that leaves some disks on the wrong peg.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Use the smallest disk as a flexible temporary placeholder
tower-of-hanoi.principle: The smallest disk can be placed on any larger disk or an empty peg without restriction, making it useful for temporarily freeing other disks.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When you need to move a larger disk but the source or destination peg is blocked by smaller disks.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Trying to move a larger disk while the smallest disk remains on top, without first moving the smallest disk elsewhere.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Place move list as the final parseable list
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Output the move list as the last list in the response, with no additional brackets, code fences, or explanatory text after it, so the parser reads the correct answer.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Appending extra text or another list after the move list, causing the parser to capture the wrong segment.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Keep move list concise to avoid token limit truncation
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Generate a short, near‑optimal sequence of moves (e.g., by using recursion) rather than an overly long list that may be cut off by the token limit.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When constructing the move list, especially for problems with more disks or complex initial states.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Producing a very long move list that gets truncated, resulting in an incomplete solution.

tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model terminates early or fails to generate any moves, often due to mis‑parsing the prompt or an early exit.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Ensure that at least one legal move is generated and that the move list is not empty before output.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Truncated move list (incomplete solution) due to token limit
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The generated move list exceeds the model's output token budget, causing the tail to be cut off.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Keep the move list concise, using recursion or other compact strategies, and avoid unnecessary commentary.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Moving a non‑top disk (source peg top mismatch)
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model selects a disk that is not the topmost on its source peg, violating the rule that only the top disk may be moved.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Always check the source peg's top disk before issuing a move.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Moving a larger disk onto a smaller disk (illegal placement)
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model places a disk onto a peg where the top disk is smaller, breaking the size ordering rule.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Validate that the destination peg's top disk (if any) is larger than the moving disk before moving.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Extra list after move list causing parser to read wrong answer
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model adds additional brackets or text after the move list, so the parser captures the wrong segment as the answer.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Terminate the response with the move list and no further characters.
